PullRequest.Title: Guard editor and group transfers across windows
PullRequest.Body:

An editor can refuse to move with `EditorInput.canMove`. Examples are a canvas, a modified custom editor whose changes can't be backed up, and the issue reporter while it captures. Several paths that take editors into another window or part didn't ask:
- moving or copying a whole group to another part;
- merging groups into another part;
- dragging a group or a tab out to a new window;
- the Move/Copy Editor/Group into New Window commands;
- moving the modal editor part into a new window.

Some of these cloned the group and then force-closed the source. The New Window commands could also refuse only after creating the window, leaving an empty window behind.

## Changes

- **`EditorInput.canMoveToNewWindow(sourceGroup)`** (default `true`) answers for a window that doesn't exist yet. Canvases (also the native canvases of the Agents window), custom editors (modified with `canHotExit === false`, the same policy as `canMove`) and the issue reporter (while attachments or captures are pending) implement it.
- **`editorTransferVeto.ts`:**
  - a pure check over the exact editors that take part, and a whole-group wrapper. A copy that copies each editor asks only `Singleton` editors. Copying a whole group into another part asks all its editors, because the copied group keeps the same editors;
  - a shared check for moving a modal part into the main window;
  - the veto dialog: its "Try saving or reverting" detail is shown only for dirty editors;
  - `transferToNewWindow`: checks first, creates the window, re-checks against the real target group, and closes the new window again only if it's still empty.
- **`EditorPart`** checks transfers into another part before anything changes, all-or-nothing, against the group where the operation actually puts the editors (`IEditorGroupsView.getTransferTarget`): a move within a part stays in its grid, a copy is added by the part of the group, and a compact auxiliary window adds its groups to the main window: `moveGroup`, `copyGroup`, `mergeGroup` and `mergeAllGroups` (all source groups first). `ContentPart` checks before announcing `onWillMoveGroupOut`. A refused transfer changes nothing and fires no events.
- **Callers** check before changing anything:
  - the drop overlay, and a group dropped onto another part's tab strip;
  - group and tab drag-out;
  - the New Window commands;
  - Open Modal Editor in Main Window (which now resolves to whether the editors moved);
  - the Agents window's Open in Editor Area for modal editors, which checks before it changes the modal setting or the layout, and maximizes and focuses only once the editors are in the editor area.
- **Only the participating editors are asked:** tab drag-out and Move/Copy Editor into New Window ask only the dragged or selected editors, so an inactive editor that can't move doesn't block moving another tab.

## Not changed

- **Moves and merges within one part** behave exactly as before.
- **Closing a window or part keeps today's behavior:**
  - When the user closes a floating window, it still asks each editor before unloading. If one can't move, that editor is revealed, the window stays open and the existing dialog shows.
  - Programmatic closes (an auxiliary part when a working set or layout state is applied, the modal part, a content part) still merge editors back one by one. An editor that can't go stays with its part.
  - Restore Editors into Main Window and Open Modal Editor in Main Window are explicit transfers, so each is checked as a whole.
- **`closeEmptyGroups`, same-window moves of editors that allow them, and editors that don't override the new hook** are unchanged.

## How to test

- **Editors that refuse:**
  - open a canvas (Agents window);
  - make a custom editor dirty, from a provider without backups;
  - with `issueReporter.wizard.openLocation: editor`, start a delayed screenshot in the issue reporter.
- **Then try:**
  - Move/Copy Editor into New Window and Move/Copy Editor Group into New Window;
  - Restore Editors into Main Window from a floating window;
  - dragging the tab or the group out of the window or onto another window's group or tab strip.
- **Expected:** each attempt shows a dialog with the reason and leaves everything in place: no new or empty window, no partial move.
- **After saving or reverting** (or once the capture finishes), the same transfers work.
- **Ordinary editors** move and copy as before, including when an editor that refuses is inactive in the same group.

## Review

Independent review rounds found and fixed four gaps in this change:
1. A group dropped onto another part's tab strip focused the target after a refused merge.
2. Open Modal Editor in Main Window went through the close path and moved some editors before one refused.
3. The Agents window's Open in Editor Area changed the modal setting and the layout before the move could refuse.
4. Open in Editor Area skipped its finishing step when reopening the changes closed the modal.

Each fix has a test that fails without it. Close paths were kept at today's behavior on purpose (see above).

## Validation

**Unit tests:** `./scripts/test.sh --runList <list> --workers 4` over every test file of the affected folders: **4001 passing, 0 failing, 3 pending**, 220 test files. The folders:
- `workbench/services/editor/test`, `workbench/test/browser/parts/editor`, `workbench/test/browser/parts/partGrid`;
- `workbench/contrib/{canvases,customEditor,issue,chatWindow}/test`;
- `workbench/contrib/sessions/test` (including the native canvases), `sessions/test`, `sessions/contrib/{editor,chatWindow}/test`, and `sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionDragAndDrop.test.ts`.

The run is on the head rebased onto current `main`, which includes the `moveGroup` duplicate-tabs fix (#346425) and the move of the reusable Sessions code to `vs/workbench/contrib/sessions` (#346421).

**Negative checks:** reverting each guard makes its tests fail:
- group transfers in `EditorPart`;
- the `ContentPart` announcement;
- the drop overlay and the tab-strip drop;
- tab drag-out;
- the New Window commands;
- the close-path flag;
- the modal command and the Open in Editor Area checks.

**Static checks:** `pnpm run typecheck-client`, `pnpm run eslint` on the 30 changed files and `pnpm run valid-layers-check` pass.

**Live checks** in Code OSS (regular and Agents windows, isolated profiles):
- **Refused transfers:** a dirty custom editor that can't hot exit, the issue reporter during a delayed capture, and a canvas in the Agents window. Each showed the dialog, created no window and left the layout unchanged; after save, revert or the end of the capture, the transfers worked.
- **Selection:** an inactive refusing editor didn't block moving or copying an ordinary tab. A selection including it was refused as a whole.
- **Restore Editors into Main Window:** refused as a whole with a refusing editor, and merged everything after a revert.
- **Repeated attempts** showed one dialog at a time. Moves within one window were unchanged.
- **Dialog accessibility:** the dialog is a `role=dialog` with focus on OK, Tab is trapped, and Escape returns focus to the editor.
- **Closing windows:** closing a floating window that holds a refusing editor keeps the window with the existing dialog, the same as `main`. Closing one with a dirty text editor merges it into the main window, still dirty.
- **Agents window:** chat windows open and close as before. Open in Editor Area moves editors and focuses the editor area.
- **Restart** restores all windows and editors.
- **Compact windows:** splits in a compact auxiliary window still go to the main window as before. Reordering groups within an auxiliary window switched to compact mode, with an editor that can't leave its window in one group, reorders with no dialog.
- **Comparison with `main`:** on `main`, Move Editor into New Window with a refusing editor shows the dialog but leaves an empty new window behind. With this change, no window is created.

**Performance:** local A/B against the base commit, alternating base and change twice. Each run used a fresh profile with 5 windows and 39 tabs over 8 groups.
- **Scenario:** drag-over sweeps, the New Window commands, typing, focus cycles across windows, closing windows and Join All Editor Groups.
- **No regression:**
  - renderer, main, GPU and extension host CPU stay within the noise between runs;
  - long tasks and segment wall times are equal within ±5%;
  - listener counts, DOM nodes and heap match before and after.
- **When the check runs:**
  - never on drag-over, only on drop or command;
  - a single-editor move into a new window asks `canMove` twice and `canMoveToNewWindow` once;
  - a group move asks each of its editors;
  - Join All Editor Groups asks one `canMove` per moved editor, the same number as the moves themselves;
  - closing windows doesn't run the check.
- **Re-measured on the final head against current `main`:** no regression; every segment is within noise. For example, Join All Editor Groups takes 3.4 s on both, and splits into a compact auxiliary window take 8.4–8.5 s against 8.4–8.6 s on `main`. Listener counts and heap match.

**Not run live, with reasons:**
- **Native OS drag** of tabs and groups out of a window and between windows: automation can't start an OS drag or create windows by dragging. The command paths that share the same check were run live, and the drag paths are covered by unit tests.
- **The group drop onto another window's tab strip:** the drag data lives in a module-scoped transfer that the page can't reach. Covered by a unit test with a real drop on a real tab strip.
- **Open in Editor Area for a modal holding only a changes editor (maximized):** covered by a unit test on real parts with the real command.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Each retry of a vetoed detach command created and retained another empty auxiliary window, including its DOM, editor part, title/status bars, scoped services, and listeners, because creation preceded the only canMove check and rejection did not close the window.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Repeated attempts to detach an editor or group that cannot move accumulate empty auxiliary windows and their renderer resources, increasing retained memory and window-management/rendering overhead.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Move/Copy Editor and Move/Copy Editor Group now reject known vetoes before opening an auxiliary window, and close a just-created empty window when the authoritative target-group recheck vetoes, bounding auxiliary windows to successful transfers or windows concurrently populated by other work.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base command path, editorActions.ts:2694 awaited createAuxiliaryEditorPart before mergeGroup attempted per-editor canMove checks; a veto therefore left the newly created empty auxiliary editor part alive. The same ordering existed for selected-editor commands. The changed commands now route through transferToNewWindow, whose added preflight calls getVeto(NEW_WINDOW_TARGET) before createPart and whose post-creation recheck closes the part while all groups are still empty if the editor changed meanwhile.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move or copy selected editors or an editor group into a new window from a command
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Resolve the selected editors, synchronously scan the effective selection/group for a new-window veto, await one auxiliary-window creation, synchronously recheck against its real target group, then perform the existing move/copy and focus. A veto before creation is now off the window-creation critical path because creation is skipped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and initialize an auxiliary browser/native window, editor part, title bar, status bar, scoped services, DOM, and listeners.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one window per command invocation, independent of editor count; zero when preflight vetoes. Editor/group cardinality only controls synchronous veto checks.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The command opened one auxiliary window before the existing per-editor canMove check. If a move was vetoed, the empty window remained alive; repeated attempts accumulated windows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required and awaited for successful transfers; skipped for a known veto. A post-creation veto closes the still-empty window.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The selected editor count for editor commands (normally one command context) or active-group tab count for group commands. Checks are O(N), while window creation remains O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One serialized transfer per command invocation; the helper awaits window creation before rechecking and transferring. There is no per-editor async fan-out or concurrency burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; veto state is intentionally checked fresh before and after asynchronous creation because editor state may change. Successful and vetoed attempts do not retain cached decisions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed call sites and helper establish exact ordering, and auxiliary window construction shows the retained DOM/services/listeners.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact auxiliary-window startup cost and typical group tab count vary by platform and user profile, but the boundary count and retained-resource behavior are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. The PR fixes an unbounded retained empty-window path and adds only bounded synchronous checks to successful transfers; the fix was recorded with its introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drag a tab or whole editor group out of the workbench to create a window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On drag end outside all workbench windows, await cursor/display geometry, synchronously preflight the dragged editors, await one auxiliary-window creation, recheck, and transfer/focus. The checks run on drag end only, not drag-over or pointer movement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the native cursor point and nearest display through IHostService on Electron.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC per drag-out completion in Electron, regardless of tab/group size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same drag-end geometry query occurred before creating the auxiliary window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before veto preflight because bounds are needed to determine whether a new window should open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and initialize one auxiliary window at the computed bounds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per completed drag; zero after a preflight veto.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One window was opened for every qualifying drag-out before the transfer's canMove result was known, so a veto could leave it empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited only after geometry and veto preflight; required for a successful drag-out.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Dragged selection size for tabs, or source-group tab count for group drag-out. Veto work is O(N); IPC and window creation are O(1).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One awaited chain per completed drag. Editors are scanned synchronously; there is no Promise.all or per-editor IPC.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. Rechecking after window creation intentionally observes state changes during the async boundary.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the drag-end call path and native host delegation are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native IPC/window latency varies, but no new boundary or fan-out is introduced and vetoes reduce window creation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. One extra synchronous preflight is bounded and removes window creation on veto; existing cursor IPC remains one per completed drag.

Scenarios.Scenario: Drop editors or groups into another editor part, including edge splits and tab-strip merges
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On drop, resolve the actual transfer target (including compact-window redirection), synchronously scan only participating editors when crossing parts, then run the existing add/move/copy/merge and associated DOM/layout updates. No check runs during drag-over.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Dragged editor selection size or source-group tab count. The preflight is O(N); same-part transfers short-circuit without per-editor checks. Some call sites preflight before an authoritative group method that checks again, but all known implementations are pure in-memory state/DOM ownership checks and the path is user-triggered once per drop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Entirely synchronous on one drop event. No async boundary, queue, or burst is added.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; current state is read directly. There is no negative-cache retry or retained map.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous linear mechanism and absence of external boundaries; low magnitude risk because implementations and frequency are bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Groups with unusually many tabs increase linear check cost, but no changed implementation performs I/O or heavyweight allocation, and invocation frequency is one per completed drop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded O(N) preflight is necessary for all-or-none behavior and does not add a realistic hot-path or boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Merge or restore all editor groups across parts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronously preflight all source groups/editors before any merge, then execute the existing batched group moves. Same-part Join All short-circuits each source by groupsView and does not invoke per-editor veto logic.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total editors across source groups after grouping, O(total editors). Explicit cross-part restore can check allowed editors again during authoritative per-editor moves; same-part merges avoid the new per-editor checks.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous serial group/editor scans and serial existing merges; no external concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache; transfer eligibility is current mutable editor state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for linear multiplicity and same-part short-circuit behavior.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Very large restored layouts could make duplicate in-memory checks measurable, but realistic tab counts and user-triggered frequency are bounded, and no implementation crosses an expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression. Added work is bounded, synchronous, and attached to explicit transfers rather than startup, render, scroll, or input loops.

Scenarios.Scenario: Move modal editors into the main editor area or a new window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Scan all modal editors before changing configuration/layout or opening a window. For main-area moves, allowed transfers then perform the existing configuration update, optional changes-view reopen, editor close/moves, maximize, and focus. For new-window moves, one window is created only after preflight and all groups are then moved serially.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open and initialize an auxiliary window for Open Modal Editor in New Window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per action across all modal groups; zero on veto.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The modal command created one auxiliary part before moving groups and could partially transfer/retain an empty window when an editor refused.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited after all groups pass preflight, then followed by a target-group recheck.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Update modal-editor configuration and optionally reopen the current changes item before transferring remaining editors to the main area.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration update and at most one changes-view reopen per action, independent of modal tab count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: They ran before the transfer could discover a later veto, so vetoed actions could still incur this work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: These operations remain on the successful action path; the new veto scan now prevents them when transfer cannot complete.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total editors across modal groups for veto checks; window/configuration/change-open boundaries remain O(1) per action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous veto scans followed by existing awaited operations in sequence. New-window creation is one per action, not per modal group/editor.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache. A second check in the delegated move command intentionally handles state changes after earlier awaited configuration/change operations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ordering and cardinality are explicit in the action and command implementations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The cost of reopening a changes view depends on its model, but the diff removes that work from vetoed attempts and does not increase its successful-path cardinality.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced regression. Allowed actions add bounded in-memory scans; vetoed actions avoid existing configuration, layout, changes-view, and window work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 30 changed files and relevant callers/implementations. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression was found. New work is bounded, synchronous, and user-triggered; expensive window/IPC boundaries remain O(1) and are reduced on veto. Recorded the PR's concrete cleanup-lifecycle fix for retained empty auxiliary windows.
